title: North Carolina LLC for Non-Residents: Cost and Steps (2026)
h1: How to Form a North Carolina LLC as a Non-Resident (2026 Cost and Steps)
description: How non-US founders form a North Carolina LLC in 2026: $125 Articles of Organization, $200 annual report due April 15, registered agent, EIN and Form 5472.
llms_summary: A non-resident can form a North Carolina LLC for $125 but pays a $200 annual report each April 15, and company officials appear in the public database.
body_html:
Short answer: Anyone can form a North Carolina LLC from abroad, with no US citizenship, residency or visa. You file Articles of Organization with the North Carolina Secretary of State for $125, appoint a registered agent with a North Carolina street address, then get an EIN from the IRS. Each year you file a $200 annual report by April 15.

What North Carolina charges

  • Articles of Organization: $125.
  • Annual report: $200 on paper, or $203 online including a $3 card fee.
  • EIN: free from the IRS.

Step by step

  1. Check the name in the North Carolina business registration search.
  2. Appoint a registered agent with a physical street address in North Carolina.
  3. File the Articles of Organization with the Secretary of State, online or on paper.
  4. Sign an operating agreement. It is not filed, but banks often ask for it.
  5. Get an EIN with Form SS-4, then open a bank account.

The yearly annual report

The first annual report is due on April 15 of the year after the year the LLC was created, and every April 15 after that. The Secretary of State says the report is due whether or not the company is actually doing business. An LLC formed in 2026 files its first report by April 15, 2027.

Privacy: what is public

North Carolina's business registration database is public and includes company officials, such as managers and members who manage the LLC, with their addresses. Annual reports filed online are available on the Secretary of State's website right away. Expect at least one name to be visible.

Federal steps for non-resident owners

These apply to every US LLC, whatever the state.

  • EIN: without an SSN or ITIN you apply with Form SS-4 by fax or mail. See how to get an EIN without an SSN.
  • Form 5472: a single-member LLC owned by a non-US person files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 each year, due April 15, even with no income. See Form 5472 for foreign-owned LLCs.
  • BOI: LLCs formed in the US, including North Carolina LLCs, are exempt from FinCEN beneficial ownership reporting under the final rule effective August 14, 2026. See BOI reporting in 2026.

Registered agent address vs business address

The registered agent address is where the state and courts send legal notices. It must be a physical street address in North Carolina. It is not automatically your business or mailing address, and many agents do not forward everyday mail or let you use their address for banking.

Banks and payment providers usually ask for a business address and for each owner's real personal residential address, which for most non-residents is their home abroad. Many banks decline CMRA or virtual mailbox addresses as a business address, so check the bank's eligibility page before you apply. See what a CMRA address is.

North Carolina vs Wyoming or Delaware

North Carolina is inexpensive to form ($125) but one of the more expensive states to keep, with a $200 annual report compared with Wyoming's $60 minimum. It also lists company officials publicly and has a state income tax. It makes sense if you, your team or your operations are in North Carolina, since an LLC doing business there would need to register there anyway. For a remote online business, Wyoming is usually cheaper over time, and Delaware suits companies planning to raise venture capital. See Wyoming vs Delaware.

The Residential Address forms North Carolina LLCs for non-US founders, including the EIN application. See LLC formation.

This article is general information, not tax or legal advice.
faqs: Can a non-US citizen form a North Carolina LLC?
Yes. North Carolina has no citizenship or residency requirement for LLC owners. You need a registered agent with a physical street address in North Carolina.
How much does a North Carolina LLC cost?
The Articles of Organization cost $125, and the annual report costs $200 a year ($203 online with a card).
When is the North Carolina annual report due?
By April 15 each year, starting the year after the LLC is created, even if it has no activity.
Are owner names public for a North Carolina LLC?
Usually yes. The public database shows company officials, such as managers or managing members, with addresses.
